cohort: 31 women of reproductive age who underwent periacetabular osteotomy and subsequently had a pregnancy and delivery
finding: This study found no significant differences in pregnancy complications, preterm delivery, or low birth weight between women with a history of periacetabular osteotomy and the general population, however, they were more likely to have a cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: With a history of periacetabular osteotomy, 53% of deliveries (20 of 38) underwent cesarean section. This is higher than the national average of 32% (odds ratio 0.424 [95% confidence interval 0.214 to 0.837]; p = 0.006).
